name: Dessert Cup Carrier Box with Insert
material: Printed paperboard outer carton with a project-sized support insert; cup and lid materials confirmed separately
structure: Hinged outer box with an internal support panel arranged around individual dessert cups or jars
intro: Group individual dessert cups or jars in one presentation carton with a support insert fitted to their outside dimensions. This format uses container positions rather than loose-food compartments or large removable meal trays. The pictured cups, food and artwork are references and are not automatically included in the quotation.
measure: Cup or jar maximum diameter, rim and base dimensions, closed height, target count and total filled weight
checks: Send the actual container and lid dimensions; nominal volume does not define the size of the insert opening.
Check support at both the container body and base, plus the space needed to lift each cup from the pack.
Review condensation exposure, packed handling and whether cups are supplied separately; no leak protection or load rating is assumed.
question: How do I specify the insert for a dessert cup carrier?
answer: Provide the outside dimensions of the filled cup or jar with its lid, including any taper or rim, plus the number of units and total packed weight. Check a loaded sample for lid clearance, removal access and support. Containers that share a stated volume may need different insert openings.
distinct: Container-sized insert positions for individual dessert cups or jars, distinct from loose-food grazing dividers and carriers for full rectangular catering trays.

name: Fold-Top Noodle Takeout Box
material: Printed folding paperboard; food-facing barrier, board grade and contact conditions confirmed by project
structure: Tapered food carton with folding top panels and a compact base footprint
intro: A tapered fold-top carton for a noodle, pasta or rice portion. The overlapping top panels create a different packing format from a shallow hinged meal tray, burger clamshell or a paper bowl. Select the internal dimensions around the finished meal and confirm the barrier and holding conditions before approving the specification.
measure: Finished portion footprint, fill height, headspace, closed top dimensions and intended packing orientation
checks: Confirm the portion using the finished carton rather than assuming the pictured ounce labels establish an available capacity.
Describe sauce content, food temperature and holding time so the food-facing layer and seams can be reviewed.
Test filling, top-panel closure and packed handling with the actual meal; do not assume liquid-tight, microwave or oven suitability.
question: Can a fold-top noodle carton hold saucy meals?
answer: Suitability depends on the complete board and barrier specification, seams, sauce content, temperature and contact time. Describe the actual meal and check a packed sample. A fold-top closure is not by itself evidence that a carton contains free liquid or is suitable for reheating.
distinct: Tapered fold-top meal carton, separate from shallow hinged takeaway trays, clamshells and cups; artwork and capacity variants are consolidated into this structure.

name: Catering Tray Carrier with Carry Strap
keyword: custom catering tray carriers with straps
material: Printed board platform with a carry-strap arrangement; board, reinforcement and strap specification reviewed for the filled pack
structure: Open tray-style carrier with container positions and an attached carry-strap arrangement
intro: Plan a grouped meal handoff around a tray platform and carry strap instead of a closed carton or a raised serving stand. The pictured arrangement combines lidded containers and wrapped food, so the layout must be fitted to the actual items. Containers, meals and carrying performance are not established by the photograph alone.
measure: External container and lid dimensions, food-pack footprint, tray depth, strap attachment positions and complete filled mass
checks: Identify every container, lid and wrapped item before agreeing the supported footprint and cutouts.
Review the strap material, attachment and any reinforcement with a loaded sample; do not assume a maximum carrying weight.
Check balance, handling method and container removal on the intended route. Confirm carton-only versus coordinated container supply in writing.
question: What carrying weight can the strap tray support?
answer: No carrying-weight rating is inferred from the reference image. Provide the complete filled mass and handling conditions, then agree the board, strap attachment and reinforcement and evaluate a loaded sample. Container fit and load balance must be checked together before approving production.
distinct: Tray platform with a carry-strap arrangement, distinct from raised serving trays, enclosed multi-tray cartons and compact die-cut cup handles.
